title: Enterprise payments integration playbook (scratchpad)
content:
Context and goal:
- Target: mid-market / enterprise payments platforms that embed LLM features: invoice parsing, reconciliation assistance, smart routing rules, dispute triage.
- Use-case angle: reduce manual reconciliation time by 40% and provide conversational assistant for treasury teams.
- Objective of outreach: get a technical intro and land a 6-week pilot focused on 1 integration (AP invoice auto-extract + reconciliation suggestions).

Account snapshot (quick notes) — QuadrantPay (example):
- HQ: Seattle, mid-market payments processor, Series B 2022.
- Existing stack: AWS (us-west-2), Postgres, Kafka, Go microservices.
- They expose partners via API keys and webhooks, likely open to embedded partners.
- Security posture: SOC2 in progress, strict data residency for EU customers.
- Potential champions: Head of Product (Elena Park), Director of Integrations (Tom Wu), Head of Ops (Marcus Lee).
- Recent news: launched SMB payouts product in Aug 2024 — good timing.

Key hypotheses to test in intro call:
- They have chronic manual work on reconciliation and claims triage.
- Their latency tolerance for assistant features is < 500ms P95 for UI interactions (but backend batching acceptable for async workflows).
- They need clear data residency and KMS integration for any sensitive payloads.

Outreach variants (A/B test subject lines):
A) "Cut reconciliations by 40% — quick pilot for QuadrantPay"
B) "Pilot: invoice parsing + suggestions for your payouts flow"
C) "Reduce ops tickets: AI assistant for reconciliation (6-week pilot)"

Cold email draft (short):
Hi Elena —
I work on partnerships at Redwood Inference. We help payments platforms (similar to QuadrantPay) ship assistants that automate invoice parsing and reconciliation suggestions while keeping data in your VPC/KMS.
Would you be open to a 20-min call to explore a low-effort 6-week pilot? We handle the heavy lifting (adapter, latency tuning, observability) and ship a small UI demo for your ops team.
Thanks,
Maya

Longer outreach (if more context needed):
- Short problem statement + one-sentence benefit + 2 bullet pilot scope + one ask for time.

LinkedIn message (for Product/Integrations leads):
"Hey Elena — noticed QuadrantPay launched payouts for SMBs. We partner with payments teams to reduce reconciliation time using on-prem/VPC LLM inference with strong SLAs. Would love 10–15 mins to share a pilot plan. — Maya (Redwood)"

Call agenda (20 mins):
1) Intros and current pain (5m)
2) Their reconciliation flow and metrics (5m)
3) Pilot proposal: scope, data flow, security (6m)
4) Next steps + decision criteria (4m)

Pilot scope (minimal viable pilot):
- Ingest last 2 weeks of invoices + payment events (sample set)
- Build adapter to their webhook for new invoices (staging)
- Deploy Redwood inference endpoint inside their VPC or dedicated tenancy with KMS integration for keys
- Deliver: a simple UI list showing matches/confidence and suggested reconciliation actions + telemetry dashboard (latency, token cost, accuracy by rule)

Success metrics (for pilot):
- Reduction in manual reconciliation time per case (target >30%)
- Precision of reconciliation suggestions at top-1 > 80% on sampled set
- P95 latency for UI flows < 700ms (can relax for async jobs)
- Cost per reconciled invoice below agreed threshold (needs to be discussed)

Common objections & suggested responses:
1) "We can't send PII offsite"
- Response: we can run the inference inside your VPC or on-prem package; KMS/HSM integration; we support token scrubbing + redaction hooks before any logs leave environment. Offer to sign an NDA and share security docs.

2) "Latency / performance concerns for live UI"
- Response: propose hybrid routing — cheap cached prefix answers served from local KV cache for common scaffolding; live model in dedicated capacity for new queries. We can guarantee dedicated pool and instrument P95. Provide benchmark report for their median sequence lengths.

3) "Vendor lock-in / proprietary model concern"
- Response: Redwood supports model variants and can host customer-owned models; pilot does not require model exclusivity. We provide exportable config and migration doc.

4) "Cost — token bill will be huge"
- Response: offer a pilot discount and show Optimize recommendations: batching, prefix caching, and quantized model variant to reduce per-token compute. Build a cost projection spreadsheet during scoping.

Technical pre-sales checklist (what I need from QuadrantPay before pilot kickoff):
- Sample dataset: 200–500 anonymized invoice+payment pairs (CSV or S3)
- Schema for invoices, payment events, and flags (disputes/chargebacks)
- Access: staging API key + webhook endpoint for test adapter
- Security contacts and network runbook (to coordinate VPC peering or private link)
- Expected query volume and peak QPS estimates

Internal asks (notes to self):
- Get eng pre-sales time: 10–20 hours to build demo adapter + initial infra config (Diego)
- Ask infra for dedicated baseline capacity quote and E2E latency estimate (Priya)
- Prepare security packet: SOC2 summary, KMS integration doc, network checklist

Measurement plan (post-demo):
- Track manual effort saved via sampling (ops logs + time study)
- Log false positives for reconciliation suggestions and iterate prompt/rule set weekly
- Weekly sync with their Ops lead to capture qualitative feedback

Follow-up cadence (if no response):
- Day 0: email + LinkedIn connect
- Day 3: short follow-up, add an insight (e.g., "we saw 38% cut in time for BlinkPay pilot")
- Day 10: share a one-pager + ask for intro to Dir of Integrations
- Day 21: final check-in offering 15-min exploratory session with eng lead

Meeting prep checklist (for me):
- Re-read their API docs and public engineering blog post
- Prepare a 2-slide pilot timeline and 1 slide on security guarantees
- Mock UI screenshot (list view with matches + confidence + accept/reject)
- Quick cost model with 3 scenarios (low/med/high volume)

Notes to self / rough brainstorm ideas: 
- Consider a pre-call micro-demo: host a short Screencast showing the UI + sample reconciliation flow to prime them.
- Could offer a two-week free evaluation with metrics commit if they share sample data.
- If they push for faster delivery, propose limiting pilot to 1 merchant vertical or one invoice type (e.g., ACH payouts only).

Recent wins to mention (short snippets):
- "Reduced average reconciliation time 37% for BlinkPay in 8 weeks (pilot)."
- "Deployed a VPC-hosted agent with KMS integration for a European payments platform."

Open questions (for discovery):
- Do they have regulatory constraints for model outputs (auditability)?
- Who owns the reconciliation UI — product or ops? Who approves API access?
- What is their internal SLA target for new features in the ops UI?

Next immediate actions:
- Send variant A email to Elena; track opens and replies (Maya)
- Book 1 hour with Diego to scope demo adapter (this week)
- Draft pilot one-pager and cost scenarios by EOD Friday

----
Scratch notes / shorthand below (raw):
- if stalling -> offer partner engineering intro call with an engineer and a security PM
- maybe use a case study about invoice parsing accuracy + human-in-loop accept rate
- keep ask small: 20 min meeting or 200 records sample
- goal: convert to PS-eng kickoff or POC contract after pilot

"TODOs (tick list)":
- [ ] Write pilot one-pager (due Fri)
- [ ] Get Diego to confirm adapter hours
- [ ] Ask Priya for capacity quote
- [ ] Prep security doc packet
- [ ] Send first outreach email

End of scratchpad.
